prompt: Heating a quaternary ammonium hydroxide (R-NR₃⁺ OH⁻) typically gives:

options.label: The less substituted alkene (hydroxide abstracts the most accessible β-H)
The more substituted alkene (standard Zaitsev product via most-stable alkene)
An alcohol (hydroxide displaces the amine via SN2 at the α-carbon)
A rearranged amine (methyl migrates from N to a β-carbon)

explanation: The bulky NR₃⁺ leaving group and the required anti-periplanar geometry force the base to grab the least-hindered β-H, giving the LESS substituted alkene — the opposite of Zaitsev. This is 'Hofmann elimination': anti-Zaitsev regiochemistry driven by steric effects at the leaving-group end.
